missed_mechanisms.name: resolve_seq — u16 wire seq → 64-bit full-counter reconstruction (§2 / TV-SEQ)
missed_mechanisms.evidence: crates/adaptive-transport/src/seq.rs:20 `pub fn resolve_seq(expected: u64, wire: u16) -> u64` (SEQ_BITS=16, half-window candidate selection, RFC 9000 A.3 specialized). PRODUCT call sites: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:34 `use adaptive_transport::seq::resolve_seq;`, :2145 `let full = resolve_seq(expected, wire_seq);` (server DATA ingest, feeds RxDatagram.seq), :2239 and :2270 (further server ingest paths). Also crates/adaptive-transport/src/ack.rs:173 `let largest_full = crate::seq::resolve_seq(expected, self.largest_seq);` inside acked_full, consumed by the client at runtime.rs:1154. Wire seq is truncated at emission: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1044-1047 `encode_data((d.seq & 0xFFFF) as u16, d.unit_id, payload)`. This is the seq-space foundation of BOTH loss detection (packet_threshold_lost compares full counters) and receiver dedup (Receiver.received is a BTreeSet<u64> of full counters); a resolution error would silently corrupt every mechanism in this cluster. Tested at crates/adaptive-transport/tests/tv_seq.rs:21, seq_and_reader_bounds.rs:40-66, kani_seq_proofs.rs.

missed_mechanisms.name: AckFrame::acked_full reconstruction + MAX_ACK_RANGES=16 / MAX_ACKED_SEQS=65536 truncation semantics
missed_mechanisms.evidence: crates/adaptive-transport/src/ack.rs:166 `pub fn acked_full(&self, expected: u64) -> Vec<u64>` is the SOLE producer of `ack.acked_seqs`, which is the sole input to sender.rs:3004 `loss.on_ack(&ack.acked_seqs, now_ns)`. Product chain: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1154 `let acked = frame.acked_full(max_emitted_seq + 1);` → :1169 Event::AckReceived. Bounds: ack.rs:36 `pub const MAX_ACK_RANGES: usize = 16;` (encode-side clamp at ack.rs:130), ack.rs:42 `pub const MAX_ACKED_SEQS: usize = 65536;` (decode-side truncation at ack.rs:177 and :193-195). The doc at ack.rs:163-166 states the truncation is safe only because SACK is cumulative and later ACKs re-cover the highest seqs. This directly bounds which seqs the sender can ever observe as acked, hence which are eligible for packet-threshold declaration and for ledger un-loss — it belongs in the loss-fate cluster as its own record, not as a footnote. The findings mention MAX_ACK_RANGES only in a note under the receiver gap record.

corrected_classifications.reason: Classification stands, but two of its supporting statements must be corrected before it is relied on. (1) The gate's activation condition is NOT 'RuntimeConfig.fec = Some'. structure_gate_fec is called from the ELSE branch of the fusion_policy check (sender.rs:3538-3543), so with the shipped default (fusion_policy: None) the gate evaluates on every fuzzy_evaluate and increments diag_gate_outcomes/diag_structure_gate_opened even though fec is None; only the final actuation to parity bytes is inert in client-core. (2) The telemetry claim is refuted: n/lost/n00/n01/n10/n11/burst_delta_ppm and gate_outcomes[7] are populated in ClientStats.fate (runtime.rs:1386-1393, :1464) but are read nowhere in crates/bench — the complete list of .fate. reads in kama_product.rs:585-615 excludes all of them. Confidence should stay at 'medium' but for the corrected reason: the decision base is live under the default config while being unobservable in bench output.
